fix.digest: By the end of December at least 7,542 people had died in Western Samoa. Later estimates put the toll at about 8,500, around 22 per cent of the population (some historians give at least 24 per cent), falling heavily on adults aged 18 to 50 and on chiefs and pastors. Administrator Robert Logan had declined an offer of medical help from American Samoa, under 50 km away. There, Governor John Poyer imposed a strict quarantine, enforced through the chiefs, and no deaths from influenza were reported.
